business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force July 1, 2020; investment protections are subject to its applicable provisions and reservations.
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since September 21, 2017; investment provisions requiring ratification are not generally in force.
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada since December 30, 2018.

Canada's bilateral income tax conventions apply according to the residence, income, and treaty eligibility of the relevant partners; treaty entitlement is not conferred merely by forming an Alberta limited partnership.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Alberta limited partnerships are principally governed by the Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, including its limited-partnership registration requirements. Alberta's beneficial-ownership transparency regime under the Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, applies to covered corporations and does not create a general public beneficial-ownership register for Alberta limited partnerships. The federal Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and regulations apply to designated reporting entities and specified activities; an ordinary trading LP is not automatically a reporting entity solely because it conducts re-invoicing. The Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, and applicable Canadian sanctions laws, including the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, the United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21, remain relevant.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Usually certified copy and, if specifically required by the recipient, Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and periodically thereafter, identify and risk-assess domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, family members, and close associates; screen partners, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, counterparties, banks, and relevant vessels or goods against applicable Canadian sanctions lists and United Nations Security Council measures. OFAC screening is not a general Canadian statutory requirement but is commonly required by US nexus, correspondent banks, or contractual policy. Apply risk-based enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth checks, transaction-purpose and trade-document review, escalation, and record retention under applicable law and financial-institution requirements. A 25% ownership indicator is a diligence convention here, not a universal statutory LP disclosure threshold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry services, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent; Alberta's official government information is published at alberta.ca. NUANS name searches and Alberta name reservations are processed through the applicable registry-agent service.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Use a name that meets Alberta's Partnership Act and applicable trade-name requirements and is not prohibited, misleading, or confusingly similar to an existing name or trademark. English or French names may be used; a French version is not generally mandatory for an Alberta LP. Non-Latin characters and transliterations should be confirmed with the registry agent before filing. A NUANS search is a search result, not a guarantee of registration, trademark clearance, or freedom from passing-off claims.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a regulated profession, government affiliation, or licensed activity where the LP lacks the required authorization
Words or expressions prohibited by applicable Alberta naming rules or considered misleading, deceptive, or likely to cause confusion
Bank, trust, insurance, securities, university, or other regulated-sector terms where use is restricted or requires consent or authorization
Words requiring consent of a public authority or other party under applicable law
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Confirm the applicable reservation period and filing procedure with an authorized Alberta registry agent before relying on a reservation; reservation periods and service procedures may change. If a proposed name is rejected, obtain the rejection reason, review the applicable naming rule, and submit a revised name or supporting consent and evidence through the registry agent. Seek administrative review or judicial review only where available under the governing legislation and applicable procedure; Alberta does not provide a universal statutory appeal route for every name-search or name-reservation refusal. Preserve filing receipts and observe any stated review deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Alberta address and service arrangements meeting the applicable partnership registration and service-of-process requirements are required. A commercial registered-office or mail-forwarding service may be acceptable for administrative purposes if the registry agent confirms compliance, but it does not establish operational substance, satisfy bank KYC, or replace records, management, and tax-compliance obligations. For re-invoicing trade, maintain reliable books, contracts, invoices, shipping and customs evidence, transaction rationale, and accessible decision-makers.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable public statistic quantifies unannounced inspections of Alberta LP registered offices. Routine registry registration does not itself imply a premises inspection; tax, customs, law-enforcement, sanctions, licensing, or financial-institution inquiries may occur on a risk-based basis. Do not represent an unsupported numerical probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Limited Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c L-16, sections 3 (formation), 4 (registration), 5-10 (limited partners and general partner duties)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; capital contributions are at the discretion of the partners and documented in the partnership agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the formation of the Limited Partnership under the Alberta Limited Partnership Act is authorized with the name to be determined and general partner to be [Name of GP]. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office shall be established at [Address] in the Province of Alberta. RESOLVED FURTHER that partner interests shall be subscribed by the partners in accordance with the partnership agreement with initial capital contributions as specified. RESOLVED FURTHER that the managing partner and any additional officers be appointed with full authority to execute all filings, contracts, and operational decisions on behalf of the partnership. RESOLVED FURTHER that this resolution constitutes the initial governance framework and authorizes all steps for statutory incorporation, including submission of Articles of Limited Partnership to the Alberta Corporate Registry and any subsequent amendments or registrations required for compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry Name Search Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform name search on the Alberta Corporate Registry website to confirm availability of the proposed limited partnership name. If available, prepare and submit Articles of Limited Partnership electronically via the online portal, including general partner details, registered office address, and capital contribution schedule.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is unavailable or queried, select an alternative name and refile after correction within the prescribed period

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry Online Filing System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Limited Partnership detailing the partnership name, general partner information, registered office, and initial capital contributions. Submit via the online portal with applicable fee and supporting declaration. Authorize the general partner to execute and file on behalf of the partnership.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application is rejected or queried, address deficiencies and resubmit within 10 business days

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Registered Office and Initial Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm and register the Alberta address as the official registered office. Appoint and register the managing partner and any additional officers with the Corporate Registry. File any required amendments to the initial Articles if necessary.
required_dossiers: Amended Articles of Limited Partnership if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural amendment filed if post-registration corrections are required

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs for business licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License for Trade Intermediary Operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; re-invoicing operations involve no physical manufacturing, wastewater, VOCs, or waste handling

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for non-physical offshore trade intermediary activities; no fire safety certification, structural inspections, or workplace clearance mandated

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); My Business Account portal at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that carries on business in Canada or is required to file a Canadian income tax return must obtain a Business Number (BN) from the CRA by registering online via Business Registration Online (BRO) or by mailing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number). Registration for GST/HST, payroll, import/export, and corporate income tax accounts is consolidated under a single BN. A non-resident without a permanent establishment in Canada may still need a GST/HST account for zero-rated export activities or if it makes taxable supplies in Canada. Foreign partnerships are assigned a BN for each tax account and may appoint a non-resident representative for correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian domestic tax law does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election; partnerships are generally fiscally transparent under the Income Act unless electing under section 216 for investment income or making a joint election under subsection 96(1) to compute income on a fiscal-period basis. Non-resident partners may use the Part XIII withholding regime or, if treaty-protected, file a waiver under section 216. Canada's hybrid mismatch rules in sections 18.2 and 18.3 may recharacterize certain payments if there is a deduction/non-inclusion mismatch arising from a foreign entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) in participating provinces; Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so only 5% federal GST applies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada during the preceding four calendar quarters (and crossing the threshold in the current quarter); voluntary registration is permitted for persons making zero-rated exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory API e-invoicing regime exists in Alberta or for federal GST. Invoices must meet Income Tax Act records requirements; CRA may require electronic records in a readable format upon audit. Ontario and Quebec have separate e-invoicing/billing requirements only for specified sectors; a re-invoicing hub in Alberta without a physical presence in those provinces is not subject to provincial digital stamping. GST/HST returns and rebate claims must be filed electronically if the business has annual taxable supplies above CAD 1,500,000.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ETA Schedule VI, exports of goods are generally zero-rated (GST at 0%) if the goods are exported by the supplier, delivered outside Canada within reasonable time, and retained exclusively for use outside Canada. Offshore services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated if the service is performed wholly outside Canada, or the supply relates to real property outside Canada, or is ancillary to exported goods. Re-invoicing transactions must meet the documentary evidence rules in ETA s.169 and associated SOR/91-45 requirements; the supplier must retain evidence of export (e.g., customs export declaration, shipping documents, proof of receipt outside Canada) within the prescribed books and records retention period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or CBSA Export Report generated through Canada's Canadian Export Reporting System (CAERS) when the value of goods exceeds CAD 2,000 or controlled/goods require a permit
Commercial Invoice issued by the Canadian vendor / re-invoicing hub showing zero-rated GST
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill indicating Canadian point of origin and foreign destination
Proof of export (CBSA stamped or electronic proof, cargo control document and destination terminal receipt)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire advice evidencing foreign currency settlement from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating and assess uncollected GST plus penalties under ETA s.280(1) if export documentation is insufficient or false. Knowingly making false statements in GST returns attracts penalties of not less than CAD 5,000 and not more than CAD 50,000 (or 50% of the net GST evaded) and criminal prosecution under the Excise Act, 2001 with fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Failure to report foreign property or taxable supplies may result in additional civil penalties and interest. A zero-rating claim can be retroactively clawed back for up to four years from the assessment date, and indefinitely where misrepresentation is attributable to fraud or neglect.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); foreign exchange administration is decentralized, with no comprehensive exchange control law administered by a dedicated FX authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Canadian dollar (CAD) floats freely, and there are no general exchange control restrictions on cross-border capital movements, dividend distributions, or profit remittances by non-resident partners. However, payments must comply with anti-money laundering (AML), sanctions (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions and Global Affairs Canada sanctions administration), and tax reporting obligations. Re-invoicing trade transactions routed through an Alberta limited partnership are generally permissible, but the transactions must be structured with economic substance to satisfy transfer pricing rules under Income Tax Act section 247 and avoid a deemed disposition or withholding tax characterization. Profit remittances to non-resident partners of an Alberta limited partnership are subject to Part XIII withholding tax on certain amounts deemed to be dividends, royalties, or interest, but the partnership itself may be treated as a flow-through entity, requiring careful allocation of income and withholding obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose statutory surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts. Exporters and trading entities may retain foreign currency proceeds in offshore or domestic accounts and are not required to convert CAD within any prescribed timeline. Payment settlement for commercial exports must be reported to Statistics Canada under the Canadian International Merchandise Trade statistical program when thresholds are met, and the underlying transactions must be documented for tax and customs purposes. For re-invoicing hubs, no CAD conversion is required on the intercompany settlement leg if the transaction is booked in a foreign currency; nonetheless, the functional currency rules of the Income Tax Act (section 261) apply and the entity must track foreign exchange gains and losses for tax purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)
HSBC Bank Canada (now part of RBC Bank after acquisition integration)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Medium, subject to legal constraints. Offshor-free digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) accounts with non-Canadian licensees are generally not accepted as primary operating accounts for an Alberta registered limited partnership because the partnership must hold a Canadian bank account for GST/HST registration, tax remittance, and payroll obligations, and banks regulated by OSFI require a Canadian nexus. Foreign fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, or Mercury-style platforms) can be used only as auxiliary settlement rails for low-value trade disbursements and must not be the sole treasury account. The legal constraints include: (i) FINTRAC reporting obligations for the LP as a money services business if it engages in foreign exchange dealing or funds transfer; (ii) the need to establish that the EMI provides pass-through FDIC/IIROC equivalent protection only if applicable; (iii) restrictions under Canadian AML/KYC rules requiring ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) disclosure of all partners; and (iv) the re-invoicing hub’s principal banking relationship must be with a Schedule I bank to maintain clearing access for CAD-denominated payments and to support commercial letters of credit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and general partners of an Alberta limited partnership are not statutorily required to appear physically before a Canadian bank for account opening. Most Schedule I banks permit remote onboarding with enhanced due diligence, including video verification, notarized corporate documents, and a registered address in Alberta. However, for the general partner entity (which is the legally accountable party), senior management and at least one authorized signatory with Canadian residency or a UBO with Canadian nexus is strongly recommended. In practice, banks such as RBC and BMO may require a physical or video interview for the general partner’s directors when the partnership is non-resident owned and the activity is cross-border re-invoicing. The mandate varies by internal risk policy; account opening is nevertheless subject to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) verification requirements, and a Canadian resident director is not a strict legal prerequisite, but lack of physical presence triggers enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership with non-resident partners and offshore re-invoicing trade flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a completed partnership agreement with all partner names, addresses, and ownership percentages; a certified organizational chart; proof of registered office in Alberta; certificates of good standing for the general partner and all corporate partners; and explanatory memorandum describing the commercial purpose of the re-invoicing hub, downstream customer invoices, upstream supplier contracts, and expected transaction velocity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction value or high-volume wire activity inconsistent with entity size and capitalization
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit audited or reviewed financial statements (if available), projected cash-flow model, list of counterparties (suppliers and buyers) with jurisdiction and business registry numbers, copies of the master sale and purchase agreements, and a treasury management policy detailing the expected use of SWIFT MT103 transfers, letters of credit, and controlled disbursement thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign exchange forward contract requests without physical export evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a hedging policy approved by the general partner, underlying trade invoices and packing lists, logistics documentation (bills of lading or airway bills) evidencing genuine cross-border movement of goods, and annual hedging limits calibrated to forecasted trade flows with commercial justification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of fintech EMI wallets or third-party payment processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the EMI’s regulatory license (e.g., FCA, FinCEN MSB registration, or equivalent), a copy of the executed terms of service, a written explanation of the ancillary use of the wallet, and the LP’s reconciliation process to ensure all funds passing through the wallet are traceable to the operating bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected sanctions exposure due to counterparty in high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Global Affairs Canada and OFAC sanctions screening reports for all counterparties, a compliance policy including an exclusion list, the partnership’s beneficial ownership declaration, and an opinion from a Canadian trade counsel confirming the goods are not controlled under the Export Control List or the sanctions regimes administered by the United Nations Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections to the Alberta limited partnership must be made through a Canadian chartered bank account using SWIFT wire transfer (MT103/MT202) or internal transfer from the partners. The payment purpose code should align with the Bank of Canada reporting and Statistics Canada International Transactions system; for capital contributions from non-resident partners, use the classification for direct investment or equity injection. The documentation must include: (i) a capital call notice issued by the general partner; (ii) a counterparty remittance instruction referencing the partnership’s full legal name, Alberta registration number, and bank account number; (iii) a copy of the executed partnership agreement evidencing the capital commitment; and (iv) an undertaking to file the prescribed information return under the Income Tax Act for transfers of property to a partnership (Form T5013 and applicable schedule). Funds may not be routed through virtual asset intermediaries or unlicensed money service businesses due to enhanced due diligence requirements under the PCMLTFA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for outbound trade disbursements are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct TT wire transfers to suppliers and logistics providers; (ii) commercial letters of credit (L/C) issued by the Alberta LP’s bank on behalf of the entity, typically governed by UCP 600, with the issuing bank as a Canadian Schedule I bank; (iii) documentary collections (DP/DA) using SWIFT MT400 series where appropriate; and (iv) XT Transfer or domestic ACH-style electronic funds transfer via Payments Canada’s Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for CAD-denominated settlements. For re-invoicing trade, the preferred rail is MT103 for high-value supplier payments and commercial L/C where the supplier requires assurance. The entity must include proper transaction narrative referencing the invoice number and underlying sale contract to ensure traceability and to mitigate bank anti-money laundering review. All outbound payments must be reconciled to the trade payable file and the partnership’s transfer pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla CAD/USD forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank or a licensed derivatives dealer, subject to corporate derivatives documentation under ISDA or a Canadian Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in minor currencies (e.g., CNY or KRW) only where a deliverable forward is unavailable, and where the notional amount is tied to forecasted trade receivables or payables
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for medium-term working capital funding, provided the transaction is clearly identified for trade settlement rather than speculative investment
Foreign exchange options (call or put) for hedging committed purchase order obligations, with premiums disclosed as treasury costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the limited partnership's registration in Alberta.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately CAD 50; the Registrar may issue a notice of default and strike the LP off the active register if annual filings remain outstanding, resulting in loss of legal capacity to carry on business in Alberta.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013, T5013 Summary and related schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 for a calendar-year partnership; within five months after the fiscal period end for a non-calendar-year partnership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA may assess late-filing penalties under the Income Tax Act, calculated by reference to the number of partners and days of delay, plus administrative enforcement measures and adjustments to partners' tax positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (Form GST34-2) if the LP is an annual GST/HST registrant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the partnership's fiscal year-end for annual filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily compound arrears interest, failure-to-file penalty of 1% of unpaid balance plus 0.25% per month up to 12 months, and escalated penalties for repeated non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on an Alberta limited partnership under Alberta's Partnership Act. Audit obligations may arise from the partnership agreement, lender covenants, court order, or if the LP becomes a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS under CPA Canada Handbook Part I for LPs required to present GAAP financial statements; a non-reporting private LP may apply Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under CPA Canada Handbook Part II.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate annual UBO registry confirmation for limited partnerships. The general partner must maintain the register of limited partners continuously; any transfer of a partnership interest is recorded contemporaneously and reflected in the next Alberta annual return. Under FINTRAC AML/ATF requirements, the LP must refresh beneficial ownership information of partners owning 25% or more on a periodic risk-based basis, including at least annually in a medium-risk re-invoicing trade.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions, distributions and interest transfers)
Register of the General Partner (identity, registered office and capacity changes)
Partnership Minute Book (partner resolutions, consents and annual meeting minutes, if maintained)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Canada Alberta: 8% provincial (8% flat) + 15% federal = 23% combined general corporate rate; Limited Partnership is flow-through so entity-level rate not applicable - income allocated to partners
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation partners: Small Business Deduction reduces federal rate to 9% (19% combined) on first CA$500,000 active business income; Alberta has no provincial small business rate reduction (flat 8% since July 2020). For the LP itself: flow-through, no tax paid at partnership level; losses (limited to at-risk amount) flow to partners. Consider Investment Tax Credits (SR&ED up to 35%) for qualifying activities if any.
